Status.note: Two newspapers reported in March 2021 that the Trianel project company and its roughly 30 municipal owners pulled out of the 1,200 MW gas plant at Uerdingen. The Westdeutsche Zeitung wrote that the plan was shelved for good and that it is finally settled. Trianel gave price falls on the power exchange and frequent law changes as the reasons. I found no later revival.

Cancellation year.note: The withdrawal was reported on 16 March 2021 by the trade paper Zeitung für kommunale Wirtschaft and on 22 March 2021 by the Westdeutsche Zeitung.

Latest Activity.note: The newest report is the Westdeutsche Zeitung article of 22 March 2021 on the end of the project.

Status Detail.value: Trianel and its municipal owners withdrew in March 2021, reasons given were falling power prices and frequent law changes
Status Detail.note: Both articles carry the Trianel statement of March 2021.

units.notes: The status moves from inferred shelved to cancelled because the owner announced the end of the project. The two articles rely on the same Trianel statement but come from different publishers.

Captive industry type.note: A Currenta press release of 21 May 2026 calls Currenta the operator of the chemical park at Krefeld-Uerdingen. It says the steam plants there supply the production plants at the park with process heat. The release does not name units NST3 or NST4. The regulator's list shows both units owned by Currenta at this site.

qa.note: GEM shows combined cycle for this 45 MW unit. The regulator's power plant list dated June 2026 shows a steam turbine with extraction and 29.0 MW net for unit NST4. GEM shows 45 MW. The list gives 29.7 MW gross.

qa.recommendation: The plant level captive value may not fit the cancelled unit.
qa.note: The trade paper said the cancelled plant was meant to supply the public grid beyond the chemical park. It was not a captive plant. The captive value applies to the two Currenta units.
